newsitem.title: UK: Allergic pet owners prefer to suffer than sell.
newsitem.headline: Allergic pet owners prefer to suffer than sell.

text.p: Animal lovers who are allergic to their pets prefer to put up with the physical discomfort rather than get rid of their furry friends, a Canadian research said on Friday.

"Apparently many people find pets sufficiently important to their lifestyle that they are willing to ignore both chronic allergy symptoms and specific medical advice in order to continue living with them," Professor Stanley Coren of the University of British Columbia said.
In a study of 341 adults aged around 40 and diagnosed as being allergic to cats or dogs, Coren found that only one in five followed advice from their doctor to get rid of their pet.
Furthermore, out of 122 patients whose animal had died, 86 replaced it with a new dog or cat, he said in a letter to the British Medical Journal.
Coren said such a lack of compliance with doctors' orders could be expected in a cases with emotional consequences.
He said people often regard their pets as members of the family, and so are willing to put their own suffering second to their pets' welfare.
